Other regional admissions include 349 in Khulna, 186 in Barishal, 183 in Mymensingh, 177 in Chattogram, 153 in Rajshahi, 53 in Rangpur, and 9 in Sylhet.

This brings the total number of dengue deaths this year to 171, with a total of 56,916 hospitalizations recorded so far in 2024.

headline_marked: ACC approves [[charge sheet against Anisul Huq]] and 3 others
headline: ACC approves charge sheet against Anisul Huq and 3 others
summary: Former Law Minister Anisul Huq is accused of acquiring 172 crore BDT in illegal assets and conducting suspicious transactions worth 737 crore BDT.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against former Law Minister Anisul Huq and three others for the acquisition of illegal assets and suspicious bank transactions.
The ACC found evidence of illegal assets worth 172.24 crore BDT and 'abnormal and suspicious' transactions totaling 737.24 crore BDT involving the accused.

The other three accused include Anisul Huq's sister-in-law Jebunnessa Begum Huq Koli, nephew Sheikh Md. Iftekharul Islam, and a cousin Mohammad Iqbal, who allegedly assisted him in acquiring these assets.

According to the ACC, Anisul Huq's acceptable income was 13.27 crore BDT, while his net savings after expenses were 8.61 crore BDT. However, the total assets held by the four accused were found to be 180.85 crore BDT.
The assets were allegedly acquired between June 30, 2000, and July 19, 2026. Anisul Huq personally holds assets worth 96.80 crore BDT, while the other three hold 84.05 crore BDT.

The ACC investigation revealed that 23 bank accounts associated with Anisul Huq and his associates had deposits of 375.50 crore BDT and withdrawals of 361.73 crore BDT, totaling 737.24 crore BDT in transactions.
The ACC suspects these transactions were used to hide, convert, and transfer illegal funds obtained through corruption and bribery.

The case was initially filed on January 1, 2025, by ACC Deputy Director Md. Jahangir Alam. The final charge sheet now includes charges under the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, the Prevention of Corruption Act, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act.
